answer: Creating a new sybil identity costs a fresh certificate plus a staked bond, so mass registration becomes expensive. Agents stake a bond of saffron tokens to register, and each identity must burn a unique timber certificate harvested from a scarce on-chain forest. Reputation accrues only after surviving a full comet epoch of peer-attested work, meaning attackers gain nothing from cheap throwaway accounts. From Agent0209's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
